rounds.title: Round 1 · truth fixes
rounds.note: Same model (GPT-6 Luna, medium effort), same picture, and the same instructions except one sentence about drawings the solver cannot solve, which none of these ten is. Four of the ten sheets are word-for-word identical between the versions, so those pairs show how much the model varies on its own.

rounds.title: Round 2 · v4: link jobs, family check, schematic filmstrip
rounds.note: Same model and effort. v4 changes the fact sheet a lot and the prompt a little (see Results), so every sheet differs. Both sides are each version's first asking; v4 was asked twice, and the second asking differs in places (the Four-Bar's second asking names wipers, the Wiper's names no uses).

Hood_Hinge.why: v4 says it is a Stephenson six-bar that resembles a car hood hinge and names car hood hinges as the use, in both askings; v3 calls it a triple-rocker four-bar and suggests windshield wiper linkages.

Cylinder_Boom.why: v4's first asking puts no part name in bold, so the panel cannot point at any part (its second asking does); v3 reads as well and names excavator booms.

rounds.title: Round 3 · v5 on fresh mechanisms
rounds.note: Fresh mechanisms: eight library templates not used before, ten mechanisms students sent with feedback (five with a stated goal), and three test cases. Both sides are each version's first asking; v5 was also asked a second time.

Aircraft_Landing_Gear.why: v5 says it looks like an aircraft landing-gear retraction mechanism and names retractable landing gear, in both askings; v4f calls it a triple-rocker four-bar and names no use.

Excavator_Bucket.why: v5 recognizes an excavator bucket linkage in both askings; v4f calls it a cylinder-driven beam mechanism and names no use.

Radial_Engine.why: v5 says a five-cylinder radial engine in both askings; v4f calls it a five-slider slider-crank assembly and names no use.

Oscillating_Fan.why: v5 recognizes an oscillating fan and names pedestal and table fans (its second asking missed it); v4f names windshield wipers.

Elliptical_Trammel.why: v5 names a crossed-slot trammel; v4f says only "two-slider arrangement". (v5's second asking said Scotch yoke, which is wrong.)

Car_Steering.why: v5 says it looks like paired windshield-wiper linkages, in both askings, despite the wheels in the background image: a confident wrong recognition. v4f says nothing wrong.

Toggle_Clamp.why: v4f says it resembles a hand-operated toggle clamp and names toggle clamps; v5's first asking calls it a slow-return crank rocker for power hacksaws (its second asking did say toggle clamp).

student-196bdb37388f.why: Only v4f tells the student that PMKS+ refuses the input at A because three bodies meet there, which is what their message was asking about; v5 describes the motion and leaves that out.

student-19bc32785b6b.why: Nearly the same note; both read the Scott Russell attempt as a plain slider-crank.

student-19afdedcc1a4.why: Both describe the structure of the stuck drawing and neither sees a Strider attempt.

student-19716c16710b.why: Both describe the two unconnected bars the same way; neither sees a door opener.

student-1943d7a31665.why: Both list the links of the stuck drawing and say its motion is unknown.

student-19a3b4a71c6a.why: The same content in different words; neither names a use.

rounds.title: Round 4 · v6: six frames, the image once, discs
rounds.note: Same prompt apart from the paragraph describing the picture. Repeats the four templates with background images and the student's locomotive (the cases the changes are for) and adds nine library templates, nine student mechanisms and one test case not used before. Both sides are each version's first asking; v6 was also asked a second time.

Car_Steering.why: v6 says a car steering linkage in both askings; v5n (the image behind every frame) says paired windshield wipers, as v5 did in round 3.

Pantograph.why: v6 recognizes a pantograph drawing mechanism in both askings and names enlargers; v5n says "a coordinated pair of path tracing linkages". (Both first answers were re-asked with tools off: the first tries had searched the web.)

Cylinder_Gripper.why: v6 recognizes a parallel-jaw gripper in both askings; v5n calls it a synchronized twin vertical lift and names no use.

made-locomotive-wheels.why: v6 says a locomotive wheel drive and a locomotive side-rod drive, now that the wheels are drawn as discs; v5n, with the wheels drawn as outlines, says a reciprocating pump. (v6's second asking said a synchronized twin-crank drive.)

student-194c3d7423a5.why: v5n says this student's triple-rocker looks like a windshield wiper linkage, which nothing supports; v6 claims no resemblance.

Aircraft_Landing_Gear.why: v5n says aircraft landing gear; v6 says a helicopter main rotor head (its second asking: helicopter landing gear). The one case where the image behind every frame did better than the image once.

Scissor_Lift.why: Neither sees a scissor lift: v5n says a two-axis positioning mechanism, v6 a vertically sliding yoke drive, and v6 also says "the fact sheet shows".

Hood_Hinge.why: Both recognize a car hood hinge (with tools off).

Excavator_Bucket.why: Both recognize an excavator bucket linkage.

Punch_Press.why: Both read it as an engine or pump piston; neither sees a press.

Shaper_Quick_Return.why: Both recognize a shaper quick-return drive.

Reciprocating_Saw.why: Both recognize a reciprocating saw drive.

student-194ec874c92d.why: Both read a press feed with a rocking lever.

student-195c83613e3d.why: Both read a rocking lever driving a slider, with pump and press uses.

student-1963530d1a41.why: Word for word the same recognition: a rocking lever driving a slider.

student-18d9e70368b7.why: Both say a windshield wiper drive for this crank-rocker.

student-196b99409ef8.why: The stuck drawing gets a structural description from both.

rounds.title: Round 5 · v7: the authors' names, the image faded and boxed
rounds.note: The first round asked blind. Until now the picture reached the model under a file name that was the template's own (cases/Bell_Crank.filmstrip.png), and Codex shows the model that path; from here the picture is sent as picture.png. Twelve library templates (eight never used), eight student mechanisms and one test case. Both sides are each version's first blind asking; both were asked five times blind, and five times with the old file names, to measure the difference.

Offset_Mount_Hatch.why: v7 says a powered vehicle hatch in all five askings, from the names its author gave the parts ("Hatch", "Offset barrel", "Rod bracket"); v6, without them, says a cylinder-operated swinging arm and names an excavator boom.

Crane_Two_Loads.why: v7 says a crane jib luffing mechanism in all five askings, from the names "Jib", "Luffing crank" and "Luffing link"; v6 says a quick-return lever drive and names a shaper (none of its five askings says crane).

Pumping_Field.why: v7 says a walking-beam pump jack; v6's first asking names no resemblance and no use (its other four say a pump jack, as the app's walking-beam match suggests).

student-196f7ddefeb9.why: v6 puts no part name in bold, so the panel cannot point at any, and calls the stuck drawing a pair of linked slotted levers; v7 describes it and claims nothing.

Hood_Hinge.why: Both "Looks like" lines are wrong: v6 a powered lifting gate, v7 a tractor front loader, though v7's paragraph calls the long link by its author's name, Hood, and two of its other four askings say a car hood. v6 never does in five.

Aircraft_Landing_Gear.why: Neither sees landing gear in any of ten blind askings. v6, with the photograph at full strength, says a helicopter rotor linkage every time (it sees the propeller); v7, with it faded, wanders: wipers, a mower deck, a window shade.

Excavator_Bucket.why: Both say a reciprocating pump linkage; each names an excavator in two of its five askings.

Car_Steering.why: Neither sees steering in any of ten blind askings: twin rockers, wipers, pump beams.

student-added-steam-.why: Neither sees a locomotive: v6 three synchronized cranks, v7 rotating display wheels, which nothing suggests.

made-locomotive-wheels.why: Neither sees locomotive wheels in any of ten blind askings. The "locomotive wheel drive" of round 4 came with the file name made-locomotive-wheels.

Walking_Pair.why: Both say a Strandbeest or walking-robot leg, as the app's Jansen match suggests; neither remarks that the two legs are half a cycle apart.

Hydraulic_Crosshead.why: Both read a cylinder moving a crosshead and name a hydraulic press ram; v7 has the author's "Press crosshead".

student-19afdedcc1a4.why: The stuck drawing gets a structural description from both; neither sees a Strider leg.

student-192954d7b479.why: Both describe the crank-rocker correctly and reach for a windshield wiper.
